stated: Expand opportunities for young people to study, teach and volunteer abroad by returning to the Erasmus Plus programme as an associated country.

source.quote: Expand opportunities for young people to study, teach and volunteer abroad by returning to the Erasmus Plus programme as an associated country.

bearing_set.reason: Re-joining Erasmus+ directly expands access to international study, vocational training, and volunteering for young people — a non-negligible effect on educational opportunity, skills development, and attainment gap (wealthier students currently more able to self-fund equivalent exchanges).

Erasmus+ historically had participation skewed toward students from higher socioeconomic backgrounds, whereas the Turing Scheme it would replace was explicitly designed to prioritise disadvantaged and underrepresented students; the switch has a concrete distributional mechanism affecting who benefits from international mobility.

Rejoining as an associated country requires paying an association/contribution fee to the EU programme budget — a concrete recurring fiscal cost that must be weighed against the Turing Scheme funding it replaces.

membership_note: O7 is the primary target; O14 and O12 each have a specific, mechanistic bearing — the distributional access shift versus Turing and the net public-finance cost of association. O13 (aggregate prosperity) is too indirect to clear the non-negligible bar given the small scale of mobility numbers relative to the workforce.
